source.title_on_document: I Can Embrace and Avoid Vagueness Myself: Supporting the Design Process by Balancing Vagueness through Text-to-Image Generative AI

paper_design_summary: A formative interview study with six fashion professionals informed the design of CLAY, a tool that pairs GPT-3.5 keyword suggestions with DALL-E image generation. In a within-subjects lab session (about 75 minutes), 10 fashion professionals each made a moodboard and a pen-and-paper design sketch once with CLAY and once with a baseline DALL-E prompt interface, in counterbalanced order. Outcomes were post-task surveys (usability items, NASA-TLX, Creativity Support Index), the number of interactions, and interviews; no creativity rating of the moodboards or designs is reported.

studies.label: CLAY user study (within-subjects, CLAY vs. DALL-E baseline)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Order of the two tools (CLAY, baseline DALL-E interface) for two moodboard-and-design rounds; each participant used both. The order was counterbalanced; the paper does not say it was randomized. Style keywords for each task were randomly provided.
assignment.quote: The order of tool usage was counterbalanced across participants.

arms.name: CLAY
arms.description: CLAY interface: vague prompt, GPT-3.5 hierarchical keyword suggestions, prompt refinement, DALL-E combination images

arms.name: Baseline (DALL-E)
arms.description: Similar interface without keyword extraction, hierarchical recommendations, or combination image generation; free prompting of the same DALL-E API

participants.exclusions: Section 5 says 12 participants were recruited; Section 5.1 says 12 were recruited excluding two applicants who did not meet the task requirements, and Section 5.2 says two participants who based their work on previous designs were excluded from the final evaluation. The final sample is three males and seven females (10), matching the 10 stated in the abstract and introduction.

ai_tool.name_model: CLAY, built on GPT-3.5 (ChatGPT) and DALL-E (OpenAI); baseline uses the same DALL-E API
ai_tool.how_used: Participants entered vague style prompts, browsed generated keyword hierarchies, refined prompts, and generated moodboard and design images, then sketched their design on paper

task.description: Create a new fashion moodboard and a design sketch from a given style keyword (feminine, vintage, sporty, chic, hip-hop, futuristic), once per tool

NASA-TLX Score: CLAY mean 29.0 (std 15.87) vs Baseline mean 46.6 (std 19.59); t-test P = 0.04 (*)

assignment.what_was_assigned: No AI condition or comparison was assigned. Participants were interviewed about their existing design process, image search, and prior use of text-to-image generative AI.
assignment.quote: We conducted a formative study with fashion professionals to identify key considerations for AI-human interaction design aimed at balancing vagueness.
assignment.locator: p. 4, Sections 3 Formative study and 3.2 Study procedure

participants.who: Fashion professionals able to take a design from ideation to the final product, with prior text-to-image generative AI use and 2 to 4 years of fashion design experience; recruited through a web community and compensated $30. This sample was separate from the CLAY evaluation sample (p. 9, Section 5.1).
participants.quote: A total of six participants were recruited through a web community where fashion professionals share fashion trends, job opportunities, and style tips.
participants.locator: p. 4, Sections 3.1 Participants and recruitment and 3.2 Study procedure; p. 9, Section 5.1 Participants (distinct evaluation sample)

ai_tool.how_used: No AI tool was assigned in this interview study. Participants described their prior use of text-to-image generative AI; the models they had used are not specified (p. 4, Sections 3.1-3.2).

task.description: Interviews about developing moodboards and designs from initial vagueness, gathering information with image search tools, and challenges using text-to-image generative AI. The authors coded interview transcripts to identify themes and inform CLAY; no creativity or diversity score on output was reported (p. 4, Sections 3.2-3.3; pp. 4-6, formative results).

eligibility.reason: The CLAY evaluation analyzed 10 fashion professionals in a within-subjects laboratory comparison of two generative-AI configurations; the same people used both tools and must not be counted twice (p. 2, Introduction; p. 9, Sections 5.1-5.2). Tool order was counterbalanced, but randomization of that order is not stated; only style keywords were explicitly randomly provided (p. 9, Section 5.2). The separate formative study involved six fashion professionals in qualitative interviews without an assigned AI comparison (p. 4, Sections 3.1-3.2; p. 9, Section 5.1 confirms distinct samples). Neither study meets the 50-person threshold. Evaluation outcomes are self-reports or an interaction count, and the formative study reports interview themes; neither scores creativity or diversity on output (p. 4, Sections 3.2-3.3; p. 9, Sections 5.3-5.4; pp. 10-11, Tables 1-3). Retain core = no and context_class = none; the paper belongs in the screening report.

one_line_finding: With 10 fashion professionals, CLAY scored higher than a DALL-E baseline on the self-reported Creativity Support Index (84.6 vs 62.9, p = 0.018, Table 3, p. 11) and needed fewer interactions (6.6 vs 11.4, p = 0.049, Table 1, p. 10); no output was rated for creativity.
